message.reasoning:
I'm double-checking the rejection sampling bound for the photoelectric angular distribution—using the batch max as the bound isn't strictly valid since it needs to be the true supremum of (1-c²)/(1-bc)⁴ over c∈[-1,1], so I need to find that analytically instead.

The looser bound 1/(1-b)⁴ is valid but gets very inefficient at relativistic energies where b approaches 1, since the acceptance ratio scales poorly and could cause long rejection loops; though this matters less in practice since photoelectric absorption dominates mainly at lower energies where b stays moderate.

I check the Rayleigh scattering acceptance test against the Thomson-like angular form and confirm the comparison logic is correctly matching the rejection condition. I also verify the macroscopic cross sections are consistently converted from mass attenuation coefficients to linear coefficients using the material density, and confirm the Compton electron recoil angle is derived correctly from the momentum conservation vector between incident and scattered photon directions.

Running a larger simulation, I notice only 7 events occurred out of 20000 photons, far below my expected rate of roughly 0.006 interactions per primary, which should have given around 120 events. I start checking whether the source geometry, position sampling, or tracking logic has an error causing most primaries to miss interacting in the volume, and decide to add diagnostic counters to trace where interactions are being lost.
